svg.text: Both legs are explained by realised chunk tokens - and they disagree about the sign
Dense (no reranker) nDCG@10 of all 24 grid configs, plotted against the median number of tokens the chunker actually produced.
Bars are 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs of the config mean (Leg A: over 10 topics; Leg B: over 260 queries). The two panels do not
share a y-axis and their absolute scores are not comparable: Leg A judges topical aboutness over ~109 relevant documents per
topic, Leg B is a near-binary known-item task with one relevant document per query.
realised median chunk size (tokens, log scale)
Leg A - TREC CDS pilot, 10 topics, document-level topical relevance
realised median chunk size (tokens, log scale)
Leg B - PMC OA known-item queries, 260 queries, judged-only rung (x0)
Exploratory, not pre-registered for inference: the 24 points in a panel are config means computed over the same queries, so they are not independent
observations and r is descriptive. What the panels license is the shape statement, which holds on both legs: realised tokens beat nominal size as a
predictor (Leg A r +0.811 vs +0.654; Leg B -0.974 vs -0.870), and chunker kind almost vanishes once realised size is controlled - the per-kind spread
falls 0.1012 to 0.0538 on Leg A and 0.0143 to 0.0023 on Leg B. The legs agree on the variable and disagree on the sign of its slope; that disagreement
is unresolved, and Figure 3 shows it does not survive the reranker.
